summary: Reproduced the current-main form of the final chunked-prefill cancellation race at both scheduler admission and delayed-result commit boundaries. Pending-abort prefill requests could enter optimistic decode and commit one sampled token plus derived metadata. The fix excludes only pending-finish prefill requests while a delayed result exists and consumes the pending finish without committing that result, while preserving mixed decode requests and packed metadata cursor alignment.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before scheduler boundary: the pending-abort final-prefill request was unexpectedly admitted to optimistic decode; 1 failed, 4 passed.
Failing-before result boundary: the aborted request contained sampled output_ids [101], and sampling-mask overflow could replace the earlier abort reason; 2 failed.

Passing-after regression and boundary cases: delayed-result admission, already-processed-result control, mixed decode preservation, zero token/metadata commit after abort, live packed-logprob alignment, and sampling-mask precedence; 14 passed, 2 subtests passed.
Extended scheduler/result compatibility coverage, including existing deferred chunk abort and speculative grammar behavior; 22 passed, 2 subtests passed.
Touched Python files compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.
The assigned single AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 executed a Torch ROCm tensor operation and returned [1.0, 4.0, 9.0]. This is an environment check, not issue reproduction.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) was visible through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015 and executed a deterministic tensor operation. The issue-specific regressions are scheduler/result control-flow tests and did not execute a model on GPU.

remaining_limitations: The reported meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct weights were unavailable, so the original HTTP workload was not rerun.
The available GPU is gfx950 rather than the report's RTX 4090; no NVIDIA/CUDA runtime claim is made.

The old v0.5.9 negative ScheduleBatch.output_ids values were FutureMap relay handles and that batch representation no longer exists on current main; the verified current defect is the delayed final-prefill token/optimistic-decode race.
No multi-rank, pipeline-parallel, or disaggregated runtime validation was performed.
No native code was changed or rebuilt.
